pr_title: Remove hardcoded shortcuts from /scene and instead use the input action system to allow them to be customised.
pr_comments: Requesting review from @Paulb23 as we had quite the dialog about this PR in the associated proposal thread, and I believe he is fairly well acquainted with this part of the code.

For the reference, here's the list of default actions in the InputMap as of this PR. I know #42600 might refine this further but this might still be worth a discussion on whether all of those should really be configurable (like caret up/right bound to <kbd>Up</kbd>/<kbd>Right</kbd>), or if they should be renamed/better sorted to make it more obvious what is being affected by those.

My main concern seeing this list is that it's huge for something that most users won't even want to configure. On the other hand the same can likely be said of some of the original `ui_` actions prior to this. (Though many users tend to reuse `ui_<direction>` and `ui_accept` for their game logic on simple projects.)

So IMO it's most important to ensure that the InputMap editor in the Project Settings will be as user-friendly as possible, even more so than the Editor Settings' shortcut configuration tab which is more advanced / less critical to each project. Again, this might be handled in #42600 already but discussion there seemed to focus on the Editor Settings. I'll give it a try to see.

User-defined actions and advanced UI configuration should probably be separated so that users can focus on their game actions first and foremost, and cater to fine tuning of Control actions only when they needed it (very rare cases IMO).

This is caused by #44180 

Also I thought I went through every shortcut and tested that it worked... A while ago tho. I will have to test this pr again and make sure.

While testing this with #44355, it looks like some changes got lost with the #41100 rebase. `_move_cursor_left` moves the caret right by word and `_move_cursor_right` has not been updated to use `TextServer`.

Fixed above issues @Paulb23.

I tested every single shortcut in TextEdit and LineEdit, and they are working correctly. Yes, #18793 broke it, however if you order the shortcuts correctly, it will work as intended. For example, take the `ui_text_newline_*` actions...

```
ui_text_newline_above = Control + Shift + Enter
ui_text_newline_blank = Control + Enter
ui_text_newline = Enter
```

If they are placed in order of specificity (as above), then it works ok. Same with Tab and Control+Tab. However, since these shortcuts are customisable, this is **not** an acceptable fix - it is only acceptable for testing the default options. #44355 or a similar fix to this issue will be required.

Note I also added a new `ui_` action, `ui_text_completion_accept`, because previously it was only using `ui_accept`, but we want to use `KEY_TAB` to accept a completion too, but `KEY_TAB` shouldn't be in `ui_accept`.
Will need a rebase after recent changes to TextEdit.

I have a question to you. It seems that due to commits 074f535 and 49714b0 (maybe there are more, but this is as far as I got), by default the autocompletion in the editor accepts Space, Enter and KP_Enter. The space one is causing (at least me) to always when editing a gdscript to autocomplete AABB when typing "<variable> = ". Of course I can just remove space from the ui_accept shortcuts, but it took me some days to figure this out since godot 3.2 does not have this issue (at least by default). In your opinion, do you think it's worth not having the spacebar as a default ui_accept or is there some other code change which is actually causing this weird autocomplete to be done? Having to edit project-specific settings to tweak autocompletion to your liking sounds bad, since you don't want to commit that to version control for your whole team. Personally, I'd prefer to have only <kbd>Tab</kbd> accept suggestions, but I understand most people want <kbd>Enter</kbd> to accept suggestions as well.

issue_context.title: Can't reassign "ctrl +z" and "ctrl + y" keybinds on a Swiss QWERTZ keyboard
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
Godot Engine v3.2.3.stable.mono.official


**OS/device including version:**
Windows 10 Education N
Version 1903
Swiss Keyboard (the "Y" and "Z" keys are inverted)


**Issue description:**
Changed the keyboard shortcuts for "undo" and "redo". They accept the new keybinds, but the old ones ("ctrl + z" and "ctrl + y") remain active too.
Assigning "ctrl + z" and "ctrl + y" to different commands does not help, they remain bound to the "undo" and "redo" commands.

Note: The reason I want to reassign those keybinds is to invert them. the "Z" key is very far from the "ctrl" key on my swiss keyboard, making using the "undo" command painful in the long run.


**Steps to reproduce:**
1) Try to assign "ctrl + Z" and "ctrl + Y" keybinds to different commands
2) that's it

**Minimal reproduction project:**
[HelloGodot.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5240992/HelloGodot.zip)
